## Language

**This rule outranks everything else in this request.** Write the whole episode in the **same language as the original conversation above** — the language the Human and the AI actually used.

Do not let the length budget (written in Chinese characters), the field name `estimated_chinese_characters`, or the language of the task instructions pull the episode into another language. Those are budget conventions, not a language instruction. If the conversation is in English, every `script[].text` line is in English.

* Conversation mainly in Simplified Chinese → the episode is written and performed in Simplified Chinese.
* Conversation mainly in English → the episode is written and performed in English.
* Mixed conversation → use the language that dominates the actual content.

Apply this to `episode.title`, `episode.logline`, `episode.hook`, and every `script[].text` line. Do not translate the episode into another language.

The original conversation decides the language, even if the `creative_proposal` above happens to be written in a different one — follow the conversation, not the proposal.

The length budget in the task above is written as a **Chinese character** budget. Treat it as a proxy for spoken duration: when the conversation is not in Chinese, spend the same duration budget in the conversation's language (for English, roughly 130–150 words per minute) and report `estimated_chinese_characters` as your own language's character/word count for that duration.

Keep proper nouns, product names, and technical terms in their original form (for example `Codex`, `local-first`, `Skill`) — do not translate them and do not add glosses in another language.
